payload.title: Do floating gummy worms remember stories better?
payload.abstract: Earlier work found that gummy worms tell stories faster in zero gravity. We ask whether floating listeners also remember more, using twelve new groups of gummy worms aboard the fictional spaceship Sugar Comet.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A previous study found that floating groups finish a tale in 40 seconds, against 60 seconds with gravity. It did not test whether listeners remembered more of the faster stories.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Six groups with gravity and six floating groups heard the same marshmallow-moon tale. One minute after each story, listeners answered the ten questions of the Jellybean Quiz. We did not re-measure story pace.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Listeners with gravity averaged 7.1 out of 10 on the quiz; floating listeners averaged 7.0. All results are invented.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Because zero gravity speeds up storytelling, it also helps gummy-worm listeners remember more.
